title: Windowed Quota Proxy with Short-Circuit Leasing to Prevent Duplicate Billing
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Problem: At-least-once ingestion patterns (client retries, transient timeouts, mobile reconnections) cause duplicate metering and customer-visible overcharges. Current server-side ingestion ledgers prevent many duplicates but still allow windows where duplicate credits are consumed (especially across edge retries and bursts).

Proposal: Implement a light-weight windowed quota proxy at the edge (short-circuiting proxy) that issues short-term, revocable 'lease credits' for inbound requests. The proxy acts as a quota-aware gate: it pre-allocates a small lease that lets the edge return success to the caller immediately while coordinating a durable commit with the central metering ledger asynchronously. If the central commit succeeds within the lease window, nothing changes. If the commit fails or is delayed beyond the lease TTL, the proxy runs reconciliation and either reconciles by releasing the lease (no charge) or by recording the charge exactly once in the ledger. The proxy integrates with existing idempotency keys when provided, and provides deterministic local tokens when absent to reduce duplicates from client-side retries.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate charge rate for retried requests should drop to <0.01% in canary traffic compared to baseline
End-to-end tests covering client retry scenarios (network blips, timeouts, duplicate TCP sessions) pass in staging
Reconciliation job detects and resolves >99.9% of lease conflicts without customer-visible billing diffs
Latency added at the p95 for successful short-circuited requests <= 10ms compared to current baseline
design_notes: Lease allocation: proxy maintains a per-customer sliding window token bucket; each incoming request consumes a 1-3s lease token. Leases are conservatively sized to bound risk.

Durable commit: proxy writes claim transactions to a fast central ingest queue (commit record contains lease id, customer id, idempotency-key if present, token counts). Central metering performs final accounting and ack/nack.

Reconciliation: periodic job scans leases older than TTL. On missing commit a) if duplicate detected via idempotency-key, drop; b) otherwise attempt once to commit via an idempotent append to the consumption ledger; escalate persistent failures.

Idempotency: client-supplied idempotency-key preferred. When missing, proxy constructs deterministic keys using (edge-node-id, client-connection-fingerprint, request-hash, short-time-slice) to reduce independent retries becoming distinct charges.

Quota interplay: proxy consults central quota state asynchronously. To remain performant, proxy uses a cached soft-quota with a refresh policy. Soft-quota breaches trigger synchronous consult to central quota service.

Failure modes: network partition between proxy and central ledger leads to increased reconciliations; we favor availability (short-circuit) with a bounded financial risk window and enhanced observability for ops.
Security: lease tokens are opaque, signed, and TTL-limited to prevent spoofing. All writes to the central ledger require customer auth context and are logged for audits.
rollout_plan: Canary: route 0.5% of production traffic for 48h; verify metrics; enable reconciliation dry-run mode to validate no net-billing changes
Gradual ramp: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with rollout gates on duplicate_billing_rate and reconciliation_fail_rate
Fallback: proxy can be disabled per-customer via config; automatic rollback if p95 latency or error rates regress >10%
Post-rollout: run weekly reconciliation audit for first 8 weeks and report to Finance/Customer Success
test_plan: Unit tests for lease allocation and TTL expiry logic
Integration tests: proxy -> ingest queue -> meter ledger flow with injected failures and retries
Chaos tests: simulate proxy-to-central partitions, clock skews, and duplicate TCP sessions from mobile clients
Load tests: validate proxy token bucket semantics under 10k RPS per edge-node and ensure p95 latencies meet SLA
Billing regression: synthetic workload that previously caused duplicates run against canary and baseline and diffs analyzed
